title: 117. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Compound Percentage Decay
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the final value after two years of compound percentage decay.
questions.question: A car worth \(100{,}000\text{ yuan}\) depreciates by \(20\%\) each year. What is its value after \(2\text{ years}\)?
questions.explanation: For compound decay, the value after \(n\text{ years}\) is \(P(1-r)^n\). Here \(P=100{,}000\), \(r=0.20\), and \(n=2\). So the value is \(100{,}000(0.80)^2=100{,}000\times 0.64=64{,}000\). Therefore, the value after \(2\text{ years}\) is \(64{,}000\text{ yuan}\). Option A incorrectly subtracts \(20\%\) of the original twice, which is simple decay.
questions.hint: Identify the fraction remaining after each decay period.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the final population after two years of compound percentage decrease.
questions.question: A population of \(5{,}000\) decreases by \(10\%\) each year. What is the population after \(2\text{ years}\)?
questions.explanation: The population after \(2\text{ years}\) is \(5{,}000(0.90)^2=5{,}000\times 0.81=4{,}050\). Therefore, the population is \(4{,}050\). Option B uses simple decrease: \(5{,}000-2\times 500=4{,}000\).
questions.hint: Count how many successive reductions must be applied or undone.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the remaining mass after three hours of compound percentage decay.
questions.question: A radioactive substance has a mass of \(800\text{ g}\) and decays by \(25\%\) each hour. What is the mass after \(3\text{ h}\)?
questions.explanation: The remaining fraction each hour is \(0.75\), so the mass is \(800(0.75)^3=337.5\text{ g}\). The alternative \(200\text{ g}\) subtracts three lots of \(25\%\) of the initial mass: \(800(1-3\times 0.25)=200\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a one-period decay from the total decay.

questions.concept: Finding Original Value Before Compound Decay
questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when the final value after two years of compound decay is known.
questions.question: After \(2\text{ years}\) of \(20\%\) annual depreciation, a machine is worth \(51{,}200\text{ yuan}\). What was its original value?
questions.explanation: The two-year remaining fraction is \(0.8^2=0.64\). The original value is \(\frac{51{,}200}{0.64}=80{,}000\text{ yuan}\). The alternative \(64{,}000\text{ yuan}\) divides by \(0.8\) only once and reverses one year.
questions.hint: Identify the fraction remaining after each decay period.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original population when the final population after three years of compound decay is known.
questions.question: A town's population decreases by \(5\%\) each year. After \(3\text{ years}\), the population is \(6{,}859\). What was the original population?
questions.explanation: The remaining fraction is \(0.95^3=0.857375\), so the original population is \(\frac{6{,}859}{0.857375}=8{,}000\). The alternative \(7{,}220\) divides by \(0.95\) only once, undoing just the last year.
questions.hint: Count how many successive reductions must be applied or undone.

questions.concept: Number of Periods in Compound Decay
questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of years needed for a quantity to decay to a given value.
questions.question: An item worth \(1{,}000\text{ yuan}\) decays by \(50\%\) each year. After how many years is it worth \(125\text{ yuan}\)?
questions.explanation: We need \(1{,}000(0.50)^n=125\), so \((0.50)^n=0.125\). Since \(0.50^3=0.125\), the required time is \(3\text{ years}\). Option B is too short because \(0.50^2=0.25\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a one-period decay from the total decay.

questions.concept: Overall Percentage Decay Over Two Years
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the overall percentage decrease after two years of compound decay.
questions.question: A quantity decays by \(20\%\) per year. By what percentage does it decrease over \(2\text{ years}\)?
questions.explanation: The decay multiplier over \(2\text{ years}\) is \((0.80)^2=0.64\). The overall decrease is \(1-0.64=0.36=36\%\). Option B incorrectly adds \(20\%+20\%=40\%\).
questions.hint: Identify the fraction remaining after each decay period.

questions.concept: Overall Percentage Decay with Different Rates
questions.learningObjective: Determine the overall percentage decrease after two successive different percentage decays.
questions.question: A population decreases by \(10\%\) in the first year and by \(30\%\) in the second year. What is the overall percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: The remaining fraction is \(0.90\times 0.70=0.63\), so the decrease is \(37\%\). The alternative \(40\%\) adds the two annual rates even though the second applies to a smaller population.
questions.hint: Count how many successive reductions must be applied or undone.

questions.concept: Original Value from Successive Percentage Decays
questions.learningObjective: Determine the original quantity when two successive percentage decays and the final value are given.
questions.question: After two successive annual decays of \(10\%\) and \(20\%\), a quantity becomes \(720\). What was the original quantity?
questions.explanation: Let the original quantity be \(P\). The decay multipliers are \(0.90\) and \(0.80\), so the final value is \(P(0.90)(0.80)=0.72P\). Since \(0.72P=720\), we have \(P=\frac{720}{0.72}=1{,}000\). The original quantity was \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a one-period decay from the total decay.

questions.concept: Original Value from Successive Depreciation Rates
questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when two successive depreciation rates and the final value are known.
questions.question: A car depreciates by \(15\%\) in the first year and then by \(10\%\) in the second year. Its value after two years is \(6{,}885\text{ yuan}\). What was its original value?
questions.explanation: Let the original value be \(P\). The depreciation multipliers are \(0.85\) and \(0.90\), so the final value is \(P(0.85)(0.90)=0.765P\). Since \(0.765P=6{,}885\), we have \(P=\frac{6{,}885}{0.765}=9{,}000\). The original value was \(9{,}000\text{ yuan}\).
questions.hint: Identify the fraction remaining after each decay period.
